tasks.short: Describe tour attractions and answer visitors' questions

steps.what: Look up the relevant point of interest in the existing tour notes
Describe tour points of interest to group members
Respond to questions and clarify uncertainty with the group

tasks.design: Configure an attraction index in the existing {DOCS} tour notes so the guide can jump to a known site reference. Keep reading, fact checking, commentary and live answers with the guide.
tasks.previous_blocker: A guide may scroll through long notes to find a particular attraction.
tasks.enabler_now: Native headings and bookmarks can link to the existing source passages.
tasks.still_hard: Adapting an explanation to the group and being candid about uncertain history.
tasks.human_edge: The guide reads visitors' reactions and turns facts into a useful live explanation.
tasks.altitude: A small navigation reduction; the guide's authority and live work remain unchanged.

reach.task: Answer questions about a shared attraction

evidence.claim: A native document index can reduce navigation to existing tour references without generating historical claims.

assumptions: This is a live commentary episode with actual occasional note lookup. It creates no routine written response, visitor-question log or tour report; none is added to manufacture savings. Notes are existing outputs of the guide's normal research, whose production is unchanged here.

The guide selects the attraction and question in s1. Existing notes supply site name, reference heading and source passage. Native bookmarks use those headings; the eight retained lookup hours include reading, checking source relevance and manually searching unindexed passages.

Only two of ten lookup hours are scrolling and navigation removed by the index. All ninety live explanation and question hours remain. Shares are unmeasured scenario estimates, and ordinary conversation is not a software send or commit.
unknowns: How often does the guide consult notes during the actual tour?
research_questions: Does the index reach the correct attraction passage without hiding caveats?

already_counted.description: Read the located passage and resolve missing or irrelevant references manually

incremental.description: Repair bookmarks when the tour notes change

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central: 2 navigation hours removed less 0.5 upkeep gives 1.5. Low: familiar attractions need no lookup or existing notes are already indexed, so keep the present notes with no additional index upkeep.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Monitor visitors' compliance with tour rules and safety practices

steps.what: Read the current establishment rules and tour safety instructions
Monitor visitors' activities and changing hazards during the tour
Remind visitors of regulations and intervene when safety requires it

tasks.design: Keep current rules in the existing {DOCS} tour briefing and retain direct visitor supervision. A native checklist cannot replace observing a changing hazard or intervening promptly.
tasks.previous_blocker: The input is what visitors and hazards are doing now, rather than a maintained data feed.
tasks.enabler_now: No new capability is assumed to replace direct supervision.
tasks.still_hard: Seeing unsafe behavior in a moving group and intervening proportionately.
tasks.human_edge: The guide can stop, reposition or address the group immediately.

reach.task: Coordinate safe movement of a group

evidence.claim: Direct visitor monitoring and immediate intervention remain human work without a validated live observation system.

assumptions: Boundary is the ordinary safe tour, including actual rule reading and live intervention. No routine monitoring log or post-tour compliance report is assumed: the task does not establish such a record and none is created here. An actual reportable incident would require its real incident-writing and escalation steps before estimating that episode.

The site operator produces the current rule sheet and the tour organizer supplies the safety briefing as normal work, unchanged here. The guide reads both in s1. Native rule headings are already directly available; reading and applying them cannot be removed by another checklist.

Visitor activities and site conditions are observed directly in s2, with no free sensor capture, camera analytics or invented structured behavior feed. No automated communication, transaction or record commit is proposed.

All shares are unmeasured scenario estimates. Zero follows examination of the actual lookup and absence of any established routine writing or send step; no deployed change means explicitly zero incremental upkeep.
unknowns: Does the site actually require a per-tour compliance record?
Is the current rule sheet already directly available?
research_questions: Does observation of the real workflow reveal an actual existing record or escalation step needing separate treatment?

incremental.description: No new system or ongoing upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: All rule reading, direct observation and intervention remain. Rules are already accessible and no existing routine record is identified for automation; no new upkeep is introduced.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Conduct educational activities for visiting school children

steps.what: Clarify the school group's age, learning needs and practical constraints
Locate and read the existing educational activity card
Arrange activity materials and the safe learning space
Conduct educational activities with the school children
Respond to understanding and adapt the activity in person

tasks.design: Configure an age-and-topic index for the existing {DOCS} activity cards. Keep group needs, activity selection, physical setup, teaching and adaptation with the guide.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding an appropriate existing card can require browsing several activities.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document categories can narrow the existing cards without generating a lesson or scoring a child.
tasks.still_hard: Maintaining attention, inclusion and safety in a live school group.
tasks.human_edge: The guide notices understanding and changes pace or explanation immediately.
tasks.altitude: Slightly less card navigation; teaching rights and work remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: A native index can narrow existing activity cards by age band and topic while the guide retains suitability judgment.

assumptions: This is delivering an existing activity, not routinely writing a new lesson or a pupil progress report. No completion log, child profile or school message is added. Actual briefing, card lookup and physical preparation are separately counted.

The educator maintaining the existing activity library supplies title, topic and intended age band as normal unchanged card content. The guide obtains the school brief in s1 and chooses the card in s2. No additional staff tagging work is free: checking and correcting the index is priced in upkeep.

The index removes only one of ten card-lookup hours. Nine hours remain for reading and manual selection, including missing or misleading classifications. Personal child information is not needed by the index, and all live work retains its share.
Shares are provisional estimates; if activities are already directly selected there is no removable lookup work.
unknowns: Are cards already grouped by age and topic?
How often is an existing card browsed rather than recalled directly?
research_questions: Does the index reduce browsing without suggesting inaccessible or age-inappropriate activities?

already_counted.description: Read and judge card suitability, including manual fallback for missing categories

incremental.description: Check activity categories when cards change

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central: one browsing hour removed less 0.2 upkeep gives 0.8. Low: a regularly delivered activity is already known or directly linked from the booking, leaving no card browsing; retain current practice with no new index upkeep.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Research sites, conditions and client abilities for suitable guiding plans

steps.what: Research site history and current environmental conditions from suitable sources
Discuss clients' skills, abilities and practical needs
Assemble the source-reference list for the existing research notes
Summarize researched topics into the guide's existing working notes

loop.input: Selected public site and condition passages with source identifiers and dates
loop.output: Draft factual notes with a source pointer for each claim and explicit unresolved points
loop.check: Guide reads original passages in s5 and checks meaning, location, dates, caveats and whether a condition notice is still applicable
loop.stop: One draft; unsupported or stale claims are removed or rewritten manually in retained time; no route or safety decision is generated
loop.why_not_simpler: A native outline can list citations but cannot summarize varied historical and environmental prose

steps.what: Verify research meaning, dates and citations; repair incomplete drafts
Choose appropriate expedition, instruction and commentary adjustments for this group
Save the research notes and working plan

tasks.design: First use native {DOCS} citation fields to assemble the existing source list. A bounded loop summarizes only guide-selected public passages; the guide verifies the notes and uses personal knowledge of the group to choose the working plan.
tasks.previous_blocker: Research notes combine copying source references, summarizing prose and making contextual safety decisions.
tasks.enabler_now: Native citations and a bounded source-linked drafting loop can remove part of note assembly without choosing routes or judging clients.
tasks.still_hard: Checking changing environmental conditions and deciding what a particular group can safely do.
tasks.human_edge: The guide connects conditions and client abilities without assuming a document guarantees safety.
tasks.altitude: Less reference assembly and initial prose; research selection and suitability decisions stay with the guide.

reach.learn: Condition verification and evaluating client constraints

evidence.claim: Native citation tools can assemble references, and bounded drafting can summarize selected passages subject to checking against the originals.

assumptions: This task includes the actual research notes used to plan instruction and commentary; they are not a new report. It ends with a private working plan. Supplier orders, traveler notices and tour delivery are not performed or given savings here.

The guide selects and captures source identifier, title, location, passage, publication or notice date and access date in s1. {OTHER} means the source website or official condition-notice category. Missing metadata is captured manually in the retained source-selection and checking work; no free clean source packet is assumed.

Clients explain practical constraints in s2; no recording, transcript or individual capability score is created. The drafting loop receives only public source passages, with no client identities or health details. The guide alone applies the understood group constraints in s6.

Test the existing native citation feature first. The eight citation-assembly hours are actual repeat reference formatting after sources have been selected, not source collection. The model removes 6.6 of 22 summary-writing hours, retaining 15.4 for construction and rewriting, plus all eleven verification hours including failed-citation repair.

Sources can be stale or contradictory; the loop cannot substitute for current condition checks or guarantee safety. All shares are provisional. Ordinary saving remains one fully retained hour without self-approval; there is no software send or consequential release.
unknowns: Does the guide already maintain references through native citations?
How much new source-linked summary writing occurs?
Can current condition notices be captured without extra access work?
research_questions: Do verified drafts preserve environmental caveats and avoid turning uncertain historical accounts into facts?

already_counted.description: Source capture, retained summary construction, semantic verification and broken-reference repair

incremental.description: Maintain citation fields and test summary instructions as source formats change

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central: 8 reference-assembly hours plus 22*30%=6.6 drafting hours removed, less 2 upkeep gives 12.6. Conservative case: rapidly changing condition notices require all 22 summary hours manually, but native formatting still removes the 8 existing reference-assembly hours; less 2 upkeep leaves 6.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Slightly less navigation and research-note assembly, with live guidance and suitability decisions unchanged.
reach: Share sourced attraction briefings with travel guides
Coordinate accessible activities with recreation workers
role.ambitious_version: A guide with better sourced preparation and more attention available for the group, without delegating safety judgments to software.
